source: វិធានការចម្រុះគ្រប់គ្រងដំណាំ លើដំណាំស្រូវ (Integrated Pest Management on Rice), training slide deck, Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Battambang province, presented by Ms. Yem Sophy, Oct 20, 2017 (contact: ysophy168@gmail.com, 012 558 312)
text: The training deck defines Integrated Pest Management (IPM) on rice as combining multiple compatible control methods rather than relying on one alone, listing eight recognized components: (1) Natural control -- reliance on naturally occurring predators/parasites/pathogens, effective only when their population and diversity is high enough and undisturbed by broad-spectrum spraying; (2) Applied/artificial control -- human-created methods including chemical, mechanical, physical, biological, cultural, and regulatory control, generally more effective than relying on natural control alone; (3) Cultural control -- adjusting planting time, using resistant/tolerant varieties, avoiding excess or poorly balanced fertilizer, and proper water management; (4) Mechanical control -- physically removing or killing pests by hand-picking egg masses, larvae or snails, or netting/sweeping insects out of the field; (5) Physical control -- light traps, sound, or color/sticky traps that exploit insect behavior; (6) Biological control -- conserving and encouraging natural enemies already living in and around rice fields; (7) Chemical control -- using pesticides only as a supplementary method timed and dosed according to real need (informed by monitoring and the Economic Threshold Level), not routine calendar spraying, since overuse can kill natural enemies and cause resistance or secondary outbreaks; (8) Regulatory control -- quarantine and plant-health regulation limiting movement of infested planting material between regions. The deck frames chemical control as a supporting tool that should follow scouting and threshold checks, not the first response to any pest sighting.
